 What is Caching?
👉 Caching = storing frequently used data in fast storage (memory)
so we don’t fetch it from slow systems (like database) again.

🔷 Why do we need caching?
Without cache:
User → Server → DB → Response (slow ❌)

With cache:
User → Server → Cache → Response (fast ✅)


✅ 🔥 Benefits
✅ Faster response time
✅ Reduces database load
✅ Improves scalability

✅ 🔷 Where Cache Sits (In Architecture)
Client
   ↓
Load Balancer
   ↓
Application Server
   ↓
Cache (Redis)
   ↓
Database


✅ ✅ How Caching Works (Step-by-Step)
🔷 Step 1: First Request (Cache Miss)
User → Server
Server → Cache → Not found ❌
Server → DB → fetch data ✅
Server → Cache (store data)
Server → User (response)


🔷 Step 2: Next Request (Cache Hit)
User → Server
Server → Cache → Found ✅
Server → User (fast response)


🔷 Simple Diagram
Request
   ↓
Check Cache
   ↓         ↓
Hit ✅      Miss ❌
 |            |
Return     DB Call
 |            |
        Store in Cache
             |
         Return Response


✅ 🔷 Types of Cache
✅ 1. In-Memory Cache

Redis ✅
Memcached

👉 Fastest (microseconds)

✅ 2. CDN Cache

Stores:

Images
Videos



👉 Used in:

Netflix
YouTube


✅ 3. Application Cache

Stored inside app memory


✅ 🔷 Cache Strategies (Important)
✅ 1. Read-Through
👉 App always reads from cache
✅ 2. Write-Through
👉 Update cache + DB together
✅ 3. Write-Back (Advanced)
👉 Update cache first, DB later

✅ 🔷 Cache Eviction Policies
When cache is full:

LRU → Least Recently Used ✅
LFU → Least Frequently Used
TTL → Expiry time


✅ 🔷 Interview Example
👉 Example: User profile
Without cache:
User → DB every time ❌

With cache:
User → Cache → Fast ✅


✅ ✅ Interview Answer (Perfect)

“Caching is used to store frequently accessed data in fast storage like Redis to reduce database load and improve response time. On a cache miss, data is fetched from the database and stored in cache for future requests.”
